description: Mo' Creatures ported to Better than Adventure! (BTA) 8.0.1 on Babric — continuation of the archived bta-team-port/mo-creatures

mods.name: Mo Creatures
mods.description: A remake of the classic version of Mo Creatures.

releases.notes:
**Every animal in this mod is now in the guidebook**, and four of them behave the
way they were always supposed to. All five came out of one round of reports.

### The mobs are in the guidebook

Press the guidebook key and the Creatures section now runs on past BTA's own
animals into all thirty of this mod's, each with its picture, its health, what
it drops and a line or two about what it does.

Nothing was broken before — the pages had simply never been asked for. Adding a
mob to the game and adding it to the book are two separate things, and only the
first had ever been done. The descriptions have been sitting in this mod's
language file since the beginning, waiting for a page to be printed on.

The figures on each page are read off the animal itself rather than typed out by
hand, so a page cannot quietly go stale when a mob changes.

One thing came out of finally seeing the pages: this mod's deer had been
describing itself in BTA's words. Both deer were filed under the same name
internally, and when two mods claim one name only one of them gets it. This
mod's deer has its own now, and the startup check will catch it if it ever
happens again to anything else.

### The pegasus beats its wings the right way

Reported as "the pegasus has incorrect wing animation", and there were two
faults behind it.

Half of every wingbeat was inverted, so the wings folded straight through the
horse's chest for the back half of each stroke. And with the original mod's art
installed — which is how most people play — the whole beat was mirrored, so both
wings swept *inwards* instead of out.

The beat is now the original's, at the original's rate: out in a single flap and
back over four, quick while flying, winding down to a stop when the pegasus
lands rather than freezing mid-stroke.

### Bunnies and mice can be picked up again

Right-clicking a bunny with an empty hand is supposed to put it on your head,
and right-clicking a mouse is supposed to leave it dangling from your hand.
Instead the bunny rode at knee height, inside your legs, and the mouse sat a
third of a block *below* the ground you were standing on — which is why a picked
up mouse looked like it was lying flat in the grass.

Both are placed properly now. Two other things went with it:

- Clicking a bunny in the grass while another one rode your head used to throw
  off the one you were carrying and teleport the clicked one into your face.
  Picking up and putting down now only ever affects the animal you clicked.
- On a server, both animals were being picked up twice — once by your own game
  and once by the server — and the two disagreed about where the animal was.

### Cats can be tamed on a server

Reported as "you can't tame cats by playing on the server". They could, in fact,
be tamed. The server knew. You were never told: no hearts, no smoke, no change
of coat, and the cat you were looking at was not even the same colour as the one
the server had. Every visible sign of a cat being tamed was missing, so it
looked like nothing was happening at all.

A cat's tameness, coat, owner and whether it is sitting now reach your game, and
the hearts and smoke are sent to you. Cats tamed before this update keep their
owner and their coat.

### Deer drop venison

They dropped pork chops, because the mod they came from was written for a
version of Minecraft that had no deer and no venison. BTA has both. The deer now
drops the same raw and cooked venison as BTA's own deer, in the same amounts.

releases.notes:
**If you run a large modpack, take this one.** 1.11.4 and earlier could stop
other mods from finishing their startup, without either mod showing anything
that pointed at the cause.

### This mod could silently cancel other mods' startup

BTA gives every mod a chance to finish setting itself up once the game is
built. All of those run from a single list, one after another — and if any one
of them fails, the rest of the list is abandoned. Every mod after the one that
failed simply never runs, and nothing says so.

This mod was the one failing. It adds its animals to every biome's spawn list,
and in a large pack it met a biome whose spawn list refuses to be added to. The
error escaped, the list was abandoned, and every mod loaded after this one lost
its own setup step.

What that looks like from the outside is a crash somewhere else entirely. In the
report that led to this release, Signal Industries registers its Vintage
Questing quests in exactly that step, so its quests were never registered;
opening the quest book then died looking for a quest that did not exist. The
crash named Signal Industries and Vintage Questing. Neither was at fault, and
nothing in that crash mentioned this mod at all.

Two things changed, and either would have been enough on its own:

- A biome that refuses spawn entries is now skipped, with one line in the log.
  You lose this mod's animals in that biome and nothing else.
- Nothing is allowed to escape this mod's setup step under any circumstances.
  Our spawn entries are worth less than everyone else's startup.

If you saw an unexplained crash in another mod with this one installed, this is
worth retesting.

### The startup audit no longer cries wolf about the deer

Since 1.11.3 the log carried:

```
Creatures audit problem: entity 'deer' has no model at
/assets/creatures/models/entity/deer.json
```

A false alarm. 1.11.3 renamed the deer's model to `deer_moc` so it would stop
colliding with BTA's own deer, and the audit was never told. The deer was fine
the whole time; the line was noise, and it cost someone real time reading it as
the cause of the crash above.

releases.notes:
A generated asset pack you were given by someone else is now switched on
automatically, instead of sitting in `texturepacks/` doing nothing.

### Packs built on someone else's machine now get used

If you copied a finished `MoCreaturesAssets` folder from a friend rather than
building your own, some mobs came out with the right shape and no skin at all —
a blank white unicorn, an untextured pegasus, big cats in flat grey. It looked
like the textures in the pack were broken. They were not: the pack was never
switched on.

The mod only turned the pack on in two situations, and both of them required a
copy of the original Mo' Creatures to be present on your disk. The pack records
which file it was built from, and on a machine that never had that file the
record can never match — so the mod treated the launch as "nothing to do here"
and returned without ever looking in the texture pack folder. Nothing else in
the game turns the pack on for you, so it stayed off indefinitely.

The reason this reads as a texture problem rather than a pack problem is that
the mod ships built-in *shapes* for eleven mobs but built-in *art* for fewer.
With the pack off, those eleven still draw correctly and simply have nothing
painted on them.

The pack is now enabled whenever one is present, whether or not this copy of
the game could rebuild it. You do not need the original mod to use a pack
somebody else made — only to make one.

| your setup | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| original mod on disk | pack built and enabled | unchanged |
| pack copied from a friend | ignored; blank skins | enabled on first launch |
| neither | built-in art only | unchanged |

The startup log now says which of the three happened.

releases.notes:
Two fixes: mounts are actually rideable on a multiplayer server, and BTA's own
deer stops being drawn with a Mo' Creatures deer's body.

### Mounts move again on a server

1.11.2 stopped a mount from crashing a server. It did not make one go anywhere.
Sitting on a saddled horse or a gentled dolphin left it planted where it stood,
and the movement keys did nothing at all.

A ridden mob in BTA is driven by the rider's own computer, which then tells the
server where the mount finished up. Two links in that chain were missing.

The first is that nothing was ever sent. There is a method a rider calls to
report a mount's position, and the mod filled in the part of it that knows about
this mod's mounts — but no part of the game invokes that method on its own. A
pig calls it on its rider; a boat calls it on its rider. Nothing calls it for a
horse. So the report existed and was never asked for, and the server's copy of
the mount never had a reason to move.

The second is that your own computer would not steer the mount either. Anything
the server spawned is treated as the server's to move: it is dragged back
towards the last position the server sent, every tick, and its own behaviour is
skipped entirely. The keys were being read and the result was being undone
before the tick was over — which is exactly what standing still looks like.

Both mounts now do what a pig does. While you are riding, your own copy of the
mount stops waiting on the server, runs its own movement, and reports the
result; the server takes that report and moves its copy to match, within the
same one-block-per-tick limit BTA puts on a pig, so a modified client cannot use
it to teleport a mount around.

| you are | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| riding on a server | mount frozen, keys dead | you steer, everyone sees it |
| watching someone else ride | mount never moves | mount moves as they ride it |
| in single player | worked | unchanged |

Affected: horses and everything built on them — pack horses, nightmares,
unicorns, pegasi and black pegasi — and dolphins.

### BTA's deer looks like a deer again

Installing this mod could leave the vanilla BTA deer rendered as a heap: body
the wrong size, head floating off on its own, legs in the wrong places.

Entity models are looked up by a name written inside the model file, and that
name is shared by everything installed — there is no separate space per mod.
BTA's deer calls itself `geometry.deer`. So did this one. Nothing warns about
that; whichever model loaded second simply replaced the first, and then one of
the two deer was being drawn against a skeleton that was never meant for it.
Which one lost came down to load order, and with the converted-asset pack
switched on it was always BTA's.

This mod's deer is now `geometry.deer_moc` and the two no longer touch. Both
deer draw correctly, and they can stand next to each other.

If you use the asset converter, the pack is rebuilt on the next launch so it
picks up the new name — expect one slower start.

releases.notes:
Riding a saddled horse, pegasus or a tamed dolphin on a multiplayer server took
the server down with it. This is the fix, and it is the whole release.

### Steering a mount no longer crashes a server

Only the person riding a mount knows which keys they are holding, so a mount asks
its rider directly — and the class it has to ask, `PlayerLocal`, ships in the
client and nowhere else. A dedicated server has no copy of it. The moment a mount
became steerable it hit that question, the server could not resolve the class, and
the error took out the update for every entity in the dimension:

```
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: net/minecraft/client/entity/player/PlayerLocal
    at teamport.creatures.core.entity.mob.MobHorse.moveEntityWithHeading
```

Sitting on an unsaddled horse was safe, which made this look stranger than it was.
The saddle check ran first, and a check that fails stops the line before the
question is ever asked — so the server never had to find the missing class. Put a
saddle on, or gentle a dolphin and take it into water, and the question got asked.

The mount now asks in a way that has an answer on both sides: on a client it reads
the keys as before, and on a server it is told nobody local is steering, which is
true and is exactly what the server-side branch below it already expected.

| you are | what happens now |
| --- | --- |
| riding on a server | you steer; the server is sent where you ended up |
| watching someone else ride | the mount moves as the server reports |
| the server itself | ordinary physics, no crash |

Single player was never affected and behaves identically.

### Affected

Horses and everything built on them — pack horses, nightmares, unicorns, pegasi
and black pegasi — and dolphins.

mods.description: A remake of the classic version of Mo Creatures.

releases.notes:
Pegasi fly. They have not been able to since they were added, and the reason
was a number that means something different in BTA than it did in beta. Feeding
an animal the last item of a stack no longer leaves a phantom behind.

### Pegasi can take off

Holding jump on a saddled pegasus did nothing at all. It still glided instead of
falling and still took no fall damage, so from the saddle it read as a deliberate
design — a horse with wings that could only come down, and only from something
you had walked it up first.

The climb was gated on being below **half the world height**. That looks like a
sensible ceiling and it is not one: the figure it came from is a bare 128, which
in a 128-block beta world is simply the top of the sky. BTA's world is 256 blocks
tall, but its ground sits at around y 130 — so half of it puts the ceiling
*below* the terrain. Standing anywhere on the surface, the test had already
failed before you pressed anything, and the wing beat was never asked for.

Riding a tamed, saddled pegasus on a platform at BTA's own ground level and
holding jump for 60 ticks:

| | climb |
| --- | --- |
| before | 0.83 blocks |
| after | 12.49 blocks |

That 0.83 is the ordinary horse's hop, not flight. The key was reaching the mob
on 59 of those 60 ticks in both runs, so it was never a question of input.

The cap is now the top of the world, and it is only there so a pegasus cannot
climb out of one. The original has no altitude test whatsoever — it simply keeps
adding lift for as long as the rider holds the key.

Gliding and the absence of fall damage are unchanged; both are intended. There is
still no descend key, in this port or in the original: stop holding jump and the
glide *is* the way down.

Black pegasi get all of this too.

### Feeding no longer leaves a phantom stack

Feeding an animal the **last** item of a stack left something behind: a stack
drawn in the hotbar with a count of 0, which nothing else in the game agreed was
there. Dropping it or merging items into it both behaved as though the slot had
been empty the whole time. Reported against a dolphin and raw fish, but it was
every feeding path in the mod.

Every one of them now clears the slot — both dolphin foods, all of the horse's,
the unicorn's golden apple, the nightmare's redstone, the kitty's, the big cat's,
and the sand that cleans out a litterbox. The bunny's wheat was the one thing
that never had the bug, and its fix is now the shared one the rest go through.

Creative is unaffected, since nothing is consumed there to begin with.

### Also

A pegasus is no longer flightless on a **server**. The wing beat sat behind a
check that excluded the rider's own client, which on a server is the one place a
ridden mount is steered from. Single player never had a client side to exclude,
which is why this never showed until it was looked for.

releases.notes:
Predators now bite when they reach you.

A fox, big cat or bear that had caught up would stand next to you doing
almost nothing. The bite was written as the `else` of the pounce, so the
pounce's dice roll decided whether the bite was even considered — on the
nine ticks in ten the roll failed, a predator in range never swung. It
could only connect on the frame it happened to leap. The bite is now
checked first and on its own.

The ranges were short too. A fox bit at 2 where the original bites at
2.5; a big cat bit at 2.5 but settles at ~2.6 and holds there, leaving it
permanently a tenth of a block outside its own reach. It now uses 3.0,
the range a bear already uses at the same body width.

Measured over 150 ticks of a mob chasing a stationary player:

| mob | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bear | 50 | 50 (already correct) |
| fox | stood off at 2.1-2.9 | connects, closest gap 1.14 |
| big cat | 5 | 38, closest gap 1.30 |
